To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Deep learning methods trained on synthetic imagery are capable of performing semantic segmentation on real world underwater imagery; (2) The synthetic imagery can be generated using a virtual underwater environment; (3) The virtual underwater environment is capable of simulating a wide range of conditions and features; (4) A post processing step is required to improve the segmentation accuracy of the initial deep learning model output

(i) Synthetic imagery can be used as a surrogate for real world imagery for training deep learning based semantic segmentation models; and (ii) the proposed approach achieves a high accuracy in segmenting biofouling on marine structures from real world imagery.

1) Deep learning techniques can be applied to underwater imaging problems, 2) Synthetic imagery can be used to train deep networks for segmentation tasks, 3) The trained network can be used to segment real world imagery, and 4) SVM based post processing can be used to further improve the segmentation results.
